does: Cooks sliced or whole crushed cloves of garlic in olive oil over a gentle heat until they turn pale gold, so that they soften and sweeten and their scent passes into the oil.
how: Start the garlic in oil that is warm, not smoking hot, or start it in cold oil.
Keep the heat medium-low and move the pieces now and then.
Lift the pan off the heat or add the next thing as soon as the garlic is pale gold.
Garlic goes from gold to bitter brown in moments, so do not walk away.

cues.text: Pale gold edges and a few gold faces, with no dark brown.
A sweet, nutty garlic smell. A sharp, acrid smell means it has burnt.

mistakes.mistake: Frying garlic in very hot oil, so that it browns at once and turns bitter.
Cooking burnt garlic on into the dish, so that the bitterness spreads.
mistakes.fix: Throw it away, wipe the pan and start again.

variant_of.differs: The garlic is kept at a gentle heat and taken only to pale gold, to flavour the oil, not browned fast.
